## About the data

Every dataset in this course is real and traces to a named public source -- the Pennsylvania Department of Health, the CDC, or the EPA. County-level figures are reported as published, including their suppression rules and known limitations. All data files ship with the course download, so there is nothing to upload.

## Labs and homework

**Labs** are worked on during each week's lab session and submitted to Canvas by 11:59pm that same day. There are six labs across the Python half, and the lowest grade is dropped.

**Homework** is completed on [DataCamp](https://www.datacamp.com), not on this site or Canvas. Each homework is an assigned set of DataCamp chapters covering the module just finished, due by 9am the day the next module starts. Homework is graded on completion, recorded automatically through DataCamp, there is nothing to upload to Canvas. See Canvas and the syllabus for the assigned chapters and exact due dates.

## Software

All coursework will require the use of Python and JupyterLab, installed locally on your own machine. The course supplies everything as a single download from Canvas: you install a small tool called [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), which installs Python itself along with every package the course uses, pinned to the same versions on every machine. Setup takes about fifteen minutes and is done together in class during Module 0; `SETUP.md` in the download carries every step with its failure modes. A separate Python download is not required, and Anaconda is neither required nor recommended -- an existing Python or Anaconda installation is left untouched.

The slides on this site run Python directly in the browser through [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org), which requires no account and no installation.
